aliases: NA62 refined measurement of the K+ -> pi+ nu nubar branching ratio (2026 update)

claim.quote: With results from data collected between 2016 and 2022, the analysis gives ${\rm B}_{\rm 2016-2024}(K^+\to\pi^+\nu\bar{\nu}) = \left(9.6^{+1.9}_{-1.8}\right)\times10^{-11}$, corresponding to a relative precision of $20\%$.

date.note: This is a CERN news article about a conference presentation (2026 La Thuile conference) announcing a preliminary value; the full measurement was subsequently posted as arXiv:2607.16413 (submitted 17 July 2026, CERN-EP-2026-214), which restates the identical central value and is now the source for the result's claim (A16 forbids sourcing claim.quote to a press release).

key_value.note: Branching ratio in units of 10^-11; stored as a bare count-like number because the ontology has no branching-ratio dimension. Confirmed verbatim in arXiv:2607.16413 abstract, corroborated by the earlier CERN news article. See key_value_text for the fully formatted value.

key_value_text.value: B(K+ -> pi+ nu nubar) = (9.6+1.9-1.8) x 10^-11, combining data collected 2016-2024 (including newly analysed 2023-2024 data: B_2023-2024 = (7.2+2.3-2.1) x 10^-11), a relative precision of 20%

name: NA62 refined measurement of the K⁺ → π⁺νν̄ branching ratio (2026 update)
notes: Originally sourced only to a CERN news article about a conference talk (press_release), which left claim.quote in violation of A16 (claim must come from the publication title/abstract or the collaboration's own result page, never a press release). Fixed 2026-09-17 during fixed-target wave-3 verification: claim, key_value corroboration, publication and publication_source_id now cite arXiv:2607.16413 (CERN-EP-2026-214, submitted 17 July 2026), 'Measurement of the branching ratio of the K+ -> pi+ nu nubar decay', which restates the identical (9.6+1.9-1.8) x 10^-11 central value first announced at the 2026 La Thuile conference.

An intermediate conference-proceedings preprint, arXiv:2604.12649 ('New measurement of K+ -> pi+ nu nubar branching ratio at the NA62 experiment', submitted 14 April 2026), also restates this value from a preliminary analysis; the later, full measurement paper arXiv:2607.16413 is used instead as the primary claim source.
As of 2026-09-17 arXiv:2607.16413 has no journal DOI yet (CERN preprint report number CERN-EP-2026-214); publication.doi is left null rather than guessed.

significance.locator: home.cern news article, 4 March 2026 (no sigma value restated for this update)
significance.note: Neither the arXiv:2607.16413 abstract nor the CERN news article states a sigma value for this specific combined 2016-2024 measurement (the abstract instead states a 20% relative precision); left null rather than assumed unchanged from the 2025 discovery-level result.

summary.plain: An update, presented at a March 2026 conference, that sharpens NA62's measurement of the rare kaon decay using more data, including runs from 2023 and 2024, cutting the uncertainty on the earlier 2025 observation.
summary.technical: Refined B(K+ -> pi+ nu nubar) = (9.6+1.9-1.8) x 10^-11, combining all NA62 data recorded since the experiment began (including newly added 2023-2024 data), with about 40% smaller uncertainty than the previously published (2025) result; presented at the 2026 La Thuile conference.

title: Measurement of the branching ratio of the K+ -> pi+ nu nubar decay
why_it_matters: Tracks NA62's continuing improvement in precision on one of the cleanest Standard Model tests in kaon physics as more data (2023-2024) is added beyond the 2025 observation paper.
